claim_verdicts.evidence: Tempo intro: "A trace represents the whole journey of a request or an action as it moves through all the nodes of a distributed system"; "Setting up tracing adds an identifier, or trace ID, to all of these events." Output of trace-refund.sh (outputs/stage-3) shows spans of four services returned for one trace id.

Tempo intro: "A span is a unit of work within a trace that has a start time relative to the beginning of the trace, a duration, and an operation name for the unit of work. It frequently includes key/value attributes that are relevant to the span itself". OpenTelemetry Traces page lists Name, Start and End Timestamps, Attributes.

Tempo intro: "It usually has a reference to a parent span, unless it's the first, or root, span in a trace." OpenTelemetry Traces: "Parent span ID (empty for root spans)". Round 2: §5 now says the script's top span names a made-up parent that was never recorded, so the general statement no longer clashes with the example.

Tempo v2.8.x architecture: distributor "routes spans to ingesters by hashing the `traceID`"; "The querier finds the requested trace ID in either the ingesters or the backend storage." Tempo architecture (latest): "When a trace ID is queried in Tempo, it returns all of the currently stored/ingested spans that belong to that trace". datasources.yml @ stage-3 lines 36-41: Tempo entry after Prometheus and Loki.

docker-compose.yml @ stage-3: OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT: "http://alloy:4317" for the four services; alloy is a Compose service (profile monitoring). config.alloy @ stage-3: otelcol.receiver.otlp grpc "0.0.0.0:4317" -> otelcol.processor.batch -> otelcol.exporter.otlp "tempo" endpoint "tempo:4317". Round 1 evidence, unchanged.

trace-refund.txt (stage-3): "publish order.refund-requested" under the request span, both consumers under it. MessageTracing.StartConsume: StartChildOf(Read(properties), $"process {queue}", ActivityKind.Consumer), called with RabbitMqTopology.Queue in each consumer, so consumer spans are named after the queue. Publish span started by OutboxRelay (Tick = 1 s) from the outbox row's saved traceparent.

claim_verdicts.evidence: trace-refund.txt: "donhang-payments: refund attempt" with two children at the same depth: "donhang-payments: POST" (> "fake-gateway: POST /v1/refunds") and "donhang-payments: publish payment.refunded". Round 3: §4 prose now names both children of the attempt, and diagram nodes E2 and G match the output.

OutboxRelay.cs: class OutboxRelay<TDbContext> : BackgroundService; Tick = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(1); PeriodicTimer loop calls RelayDueAsync, which claims rows WHERE published_at IS NULL and starts one publish span per row (MessageTracing.StartPublish). Supports "a background loop that publishes saved outbox rows about once a second" and "next pass". OTel Traces: consumer spans "may start long after the producer span has already ended."

trace-refund.sh @ stage-3 lines 21-24: "It carries a traceparent made up here, so that this script knows the trace id to ask Tempo for; without one, the api would make up the trace id itself." tempo.sh new_traceparent: random trace id and random parent span id. Line 26 curl -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}'; line 27 Authorization: Bearer $token, token for anh.tran@example.com = customer 1 (db/seed.sql l.17).

tempo.sh wait_for_spans: loop of 60 x sleep 2; returns when [ "$now" -ge "$2" ] && [ "$now" = "$last" ]. trace-refund.sh @ stage-3 line 36: wait_for_spans "$(trace_id "$traceparent")" 20 (excerpt lines 24-38 confirm). Round 1 evidence, unchanged.

tempo.sh print_trace_tree: line = ("  " * $depth) + $span.service + ": " + $span.name + "  (N SQL)" when sql_count > 0; sql: ($scope == "Npgsql"); children() excludes .sql spans; roots are spans whose parent id is not among the returned ids, which is why the api span (parent = new_traceparent's random span id) prints at the top.

trace-refund.txt: "  -> 202" then 11 span lines from donhang-api, donhang-notifications, donhang-payments, fake-gateway. SQL counts 5+1+2+4+1 = 13; 11 + 13 = 24 >= 20. Lesson output block matches the file line for line.

datasources.yml @ stage-3: Prometheus (line 7), Loki (line 16), Tempo lines 37-41: uid tempo, url http://tempo:3200; comment: "Explore → Tempo finds a trace by its id and draws its spans as a tree on a timeline." tempo.sh tempo_trace queries http://tempo:3200/api/traces/. Round 3 §6 wording ("Grafana's Explore page with Tempo chosen as the data source") matches this comment.

OpenTelemetry Traces: "A span represents a unit of work or operation." Tempo intro: span is "a unit of work within a trace". Captured trace has 11 non-SQL spans + SQL counts, no per-method spans. Round 1 evidence, unchanged.
